1	---
2	name: utk-tool-gotchas
3	description: Non-obvious behaviors of the UTK 0.8.9 toolkit when building the *utk* trial variants (app1-app5)
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: reference
7	  originSessionId: 94f7a7ed-da40-4ad9-8678-ffa8fd3b5831
8	---
9	
10	UTK 0.8.9 (`pip install utk`, installed at `~/.local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/utk`) quirks discovered while building the noise-pollution utk trial:
11	
12	- **Overpass HTTP 406**: UTK calls `overpass.API()` with no User-Agent; the public Overpass servers now reject that with 406. Fix BEFORE `import utk`:
13	  `overpass.API._headers = {"User-Agent": "...", "Accept-Charset": "utf-8;q=0.7,*;q=0.7"}`. Also bump `overpass.API._timeout` and consider `overpass.API._endpoint = "https://overpass.kumi.systems/api/interpreter"`; wrap `_get_from_overpass` with backoff on `MultipleRequestsError`(429)/`ServerLoadError`(504).
14	- **`utk.OSM.load("Manhattan Island", ...)`** geocodes via Nominatim to a *bounding box* (not a clipped polygon), so it pulls ~59.5k buildings (incl. off-island within the rect). Per-building triangulation is pure-Python and slow: ~8 it/s → full island ≈ 2–2.5 h one-time build. A small bbox (`[40.70,-74.015,40.71,-74.005]`) builds in <1 min for validation.
15	- **Surface layer** from `OSM.load` is `type=HEATMAP_LAYER`, which the frontend refuses to PICK ("PICKING shader is not supported for the heatmap layer"). Convert it to `TRIANGLES_3D_LAYER` to make it pickable.
16	- **Picking** requires the layer JSON `renderStyle` to include `"PICKING"` (the server's auto-add route is commented out). PICKING must be preceded by a valid **auxiliary** shader (see detailed line below): base triangle layers `["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP","PICKING"]`; abstract-colored buildings `["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP_TEX","PICKING"]`. (`FLAT_COLOR` is NOT a valid auxiliary — earlier note was wrong.)
17	- **`/linkLayers`** expects **lowercase** `outLevel`/`inLevel` (`objects`,`coordinates`) even though grammar.json uses uppercase (`OBJECTS`,`COORDINATES`); the frontend lowercases them. Manual curl with uppercase → `KeyError: 'OBJECTS'` (HTTP 500).
18	- **"count within radius" is NOT expressible in the grammar**: `max_distance` only works with `NEAREST` (1:1 `sjoin_nearest`). Precompute per-building counts in Python, write a thematic layer of building centroids (coords from `buildings.json` `sectionFootprint`, in EPSG:3395), and join `NEAREST` (`abstract`, `AVG`) → each building gets its own value (centroid is inside its own footprint, distance 0).
19	- Frontend served by `utk start --data ./data` on **localhost:5001** (Flask + prebuilt React bundle at `site-packages/utk-frontend/build/utk-app`). There is no npm/vite/tsc project — generic "port 3005 / npm build" validation steps don't apply.
20	- **`utk start -p/--port` is broken**: argparse declares `--port nargs=1`, so passing it yields `port=[5001]` (a list) → Flask `int(port)` → `TypeError: int() argument ... not 'list'`. Default (no flag) is the string `'5001'` and works. So NEVER pass `--port`; to change port edit `port=5001` in `utk_server.py`.
21	- **The sandbox/harness kills any live listening server** (utk start binds a socket) with signal 16 → bash tool exits **144**, even with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` and even inside a Python `subprocess`/`nohup … &`. A fast-crashing `utk start` (e.g. the `--port` bug) exits cleanly with its traceback; only a *successfully running* server triggers the kill. ⇒ live `curl http://localhost:5001` validation is impossible here. Validate statically instead: `utk` imports, every `*.json` parses, grammar layer refs all resolve to files, and `buildings_joined.json` `inValues` length == `buildings_coordinates.data` bytes/8/3 (per-vertex count).
22	- **Reuse the prebuilt island data**: app1's full build lives at `app1-subway-accessibility/t3/utk/output/data` (10141 buildings, 7,462,756 building vertices, ~447 MB) — copy the physical layers (buildings/surface/parks/water/roads `.json`+`.data`) rather than re-running the 2–2.5 h OSM build. That build already ships `buildings.json renderStyle=["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP_TEX","PICKING"]`. Copy only the physical layers; regenerate `grammar.json`, the thematic layer, and `buildings_joined.json`.
23	- **Replicating the COORDINATES3D NEAREST join in pure numpy is byte-identical to UTK and ~1000× faster.** UTK's `attachLayers` coordinates3d path = `scipy.spatial.KDTree(centroids).query(building_vertices,1)`, `inValues[vertex]=centroid_value[nearest]` (single neighbor ⇒ avg/sum/min/max all = the value). Verified `np.array_equal` vs the shipped `buildings_joined.json` (0 mismatches, 3 s vs UTK's multi-minute pandas `.iloc` loop). So: build centroids (mean of `buildings.json[i].sectionFootprint[0]`, EPSG:3395), precompute per-building values, write thematic `{"id","coordinates":[x,y,z,...],"values":[...]}`, then write `buildings_joined.json` = `{"joinedLayers":[{"spatial_relation":"NEAREST","layerId":<id>,"outLevel":"COORDINATES3D","inLevel":"COORDINATES3D","abstract":true}],"joinedObjects":[{"joinedLayerIndex":0,"inValues":[...per-vertex...]}]}`. inValues length must == `buildings_coordinates.data` bytes/8/3. (A naive per-building broadcast does NOT match — ~14% of vertices map to a neighbor's centroid; use the KDTree.)
24	- **The live server CAN run and be curl'd in this harness after all** (contradicts the old "exits 144" note for at least some sessions): `utk start --data ./data` ran a full 25 s under `timeout` (exit 124, not killed) and served HTTP 200. Data is NOT at `/data/...`; the real routes (`utk_server.py`) are: `/` + `/main.js` + `/main.*.css` (prebuilt React bundle), `/getGrammar`, `/getLayer?layer=<name>` (reads `<workdir>/<name>.json`), `/files/<path>` (raw files incl. `*.data`, `*_joined.json`), `/linkLayers`, `/solveNominatim`. Validate live by curling `/getGrammar`, `/getLayer?layer=buildings`, `/files/buildings_joined.json`, `/main.js`.
25	- **Picking on all 5 layers** needs grammar `interactions:["PICKING",...]` (one per knot) + each layer `renderStyle` ending in `PICKING` **preceded by a valid auxiliary shader** (order matters). CORRECTION to an earlier wrong note: `FLAT_COLOR` does NOT work as the picking auxiliary — runtime throws "The shader picking needs an auxiliary shader... SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP can be used". Verified in the bundle via paren-matching: `ShaderFlatColor extends Shader` (invalid); for a `TRIANGLES_3D_LAYER` the aux must be `ShaderSmoothColorMap extends AuxiliaryShaderTriangles`, for a `BUILDINGS_LAYER` `ShaderSmoothColorMapTex extends AuxiliaryShader`. So: base triangle layers (surface/water/parks/roads) = `["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP","PICKING"]`; buildings = `["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP_TEX","PICKING"]`. Surface must also be flipped `HEATMAP_LAYER`→`TRIANGLES_3D_LAYER` (drop `discardFuncInterval`). Pure knots are `{"id","colorMap"?,"integration_scheme":[{"out":{"name","level":"OBJECTS"}}]}`.
26	- **A pickable triangle base layer MUST carry abstract function data, or it crashes at load.** `ShaderSmoothColorMap.updateShaderData` (the triangle-layer renderer, which is also the only `AuxiliaryShaderTriangles`, so it's mandatory for triangle picking) does `d3.extent(this._function[this._functionToUse])` with NO empty-guard. A *pure* knot (just `out`/OBJECTS, no `in`/abstract) leaves the function array empty ⇒ `this._function[0]` undefined ⇒ "Uncaught TypeError: undefined is not iterable (Symbol.iterator)" — the error surfaces right after the buildings geometry fetch because ALL layer geometry loads before the per-knot shader pass runs (knot order: base layers first). NOTE: `ShaderSmoothColorMapTex` (buildings) iterates `r.length` and is safe with empty data, so buildings are NOT the culprit despite the network/stack appearing to point there. FIX: give each base triangle layer a **constant OBJECTS-level abstract join**: write `<layer>Theme.json` (`{id,coordinates,values}`, one centroid+value per object) + `<layer>_joined.json` (`joinedLayers:[{spatial_relation:"NEAREST",layerId:"<layer>Theme",outLevel:"OBJECTS",inLevel:"COORDINATES",abstract:true}]`, `joinedObjects:[{joinedLayerIndex:0,inValues:[const]*numObjects}]`) and make the knot abstract (`in:{name:"<layer>Theme",level:"COORDINATES"}, out:{name:"<layer>",level:"OBJECTS"}`). The frontend (`getAbstractDataFromLink` OBJECTS branch) expands `inValues[obj]` across that object's coords via `getCoordsPerComp`; `TrianglesLayer.distributeFunctionValues` is identity. A **constant** value is robust: d3 `scaleLinear` with a degenerate domain `[v,v]` returns `0.5` for all (NOT NaN), so every element renders flat `colorMap(0.5)` — pick Greys(mid-grey)/Blues(mid-blue)/Greens(mid-green) for natural map tones. `in`/theme layers are referenced only by the join match (`getJoinedObjects`: `layerId==in.name && in.level==inLevel && spatial_relation && out.level==outLevel && abstract`), are NOT in the map's load loop (which only loads `out.name`s), but the file should still exist. A **picked element is drawn blue** `vec4(0,0,1,1)` (satisfies "color changes on click").
27	- **Picking needs a per-triangle `ids` buffer** (`<layer>_ids.data`, uint32, one id per triangle = `numIndices/3`, referenced `[start,size]` per data entry). `OSM.load` emits ids for buildings+surface but NOT water/parks/roads → those must be generated or picking selects nothing. ids are **component-local**: the frontend offsets each component's ids by the cumulative vertex count (`getIdsVBO`: `id+t, t+=nVertex`), so writing all-zero local ids makes each data entry (one OSM feature) a single globally-unique selectable cell. Buildings instead use many distinct local ids per building for sub-footprint picking.
28	- **LINKED scatterplot / plots + brushing (app3)**: grammar `plots:[{plot:<vega-lite v5 spec, NO data field>, knots:[...], arrangement:"LINKED", interaction:"CLICK"}]`. The frontend (`attachPlots`/`proccessKnotData`) builds, per knot, rows `{<knotId>_index,<knotId>_abstract,<knotId>_highlight}`; multiple plot knots are **merged row-by-row** (must be equal length & aligned) so a scatter can reference `knotA_abstract` (x) and `knotB_abstract` (y). **`interaction:"BRUSH"` THROWS "Plot BRUSH not implemented yet"** in 0.8.9 — only `CLICK`/`HOVER` are wired to map highlight. So implement "brush points→highlight buildings" with `CLICK` (toggles per-point selection, highlights the building blue). KEY: the plot knot that drives highlight must be the **rendered** map knot (in `map.knots`), else the highlight writes to a non-rendered shader and is invisible — so make the x-knot (per-building noise, OBJECTS) BOTH the map color knot AND scatter x; the y-knot (area) is plot-only (in component `knots` but not `map.knots` — `initKnots` runs `processThematicData`+`loadShaders` for ALL component knots regardless). One point per building ⇒ knots at **OBJECTS** level: buildings supports an OBJECTS abstract join (`getAbstractDataFromLink` OBJECTS branch expands each object's single `inValue` across its vertices via `getCoordsPerComp`; `inValues` length must == #buildings = #mesh components). Put MULTIPLE joins in one `buildings_joined.json` (`joinedLayers[]`+`joinedObjects[]`), matched by (`layerId`==in.name, inLevel, outLevel, spatial_relation, abstract). Building **area**: shoelace on `sectionFootprint[0]` reprojected 3395→32618 (3395 area distorted ~1.74× at 40.7°). Live `utk start --data ./data` validates fine under `timeout` (routes `/getGrammar`,`/getLayer?layer=`,`/files/*` all 200) — but watch for a **stale prior utk server holding :5001** ("Address already in use"): `ss -ltnp|grep 5001` then `kill`.
29	- **Roads / street-network (app4)**: roads are a `TRIANGLES_3D_LAYER` — UTK `osm_to_roads_polyline` takes each OSM way, intersects with the island poly, then **buffers each centre-line by 2 m and earcut-triangulates it**, so the per-feature mesh is a thin polygon outline and the centre-line *length cannot be recovered from the mesh*. To get aligned lengths: **monkeypatch `OSM.osm_to_roads_polyline`** to re-derive `inter_parts` from the same `osm_elements`/`bpoly` (deterministic same order as the mesh — verified `len(centerlines)==len(mesh.data)`, 20642 for full island) and measure each `LineString` in EPSG:32618 (true metres; 3395 length inflated ~1.32×). Colour roads by length via an **OBJECTS abstract NEAREST join** (one value/road, like the app3 buildings pattern; `renderStyle=["SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP","PICKING"]`). Two interchangeable colourings (length + noise-within-10m) = two knots on the same `roads` layer, both joins in one `roads_joined.json`, switched with the `TOGGLE_KNOT` widget. **Full-island load WITHOUT buildings is fast (~45 s)** (no per-building Python triangulation) — surface/water/parks/roads only; passing the island *polygon* to `OSM.load` clips roads to the island. ids/picking for water/parks/roads: generate `<layer>_ids.data` (all-zero local uint32, one per triangle, `ids:[start,size]` per feature) since `OSM.load` emits ids only for buildings+surface. **Built app4 t2 utk** at `app4-street-network/t2/utk/output` (`build_data.py` + `data/`): two OBJECTS knots on `roads` (`roadLength` viridis / `roadNoise` inferno) both in `map.knots`, switched by `TOGGLE_KNOT`; `noise within 10m` via `shapely.STRtree.query(pt,predicate="dwithin",distance=10)` accumulated per segment (max 36, 1843 segs >=1). NOTE: the **string** `OSM.load("Manhattan Island")` (Nominatim→bbox, NOT polygon-clipped) yielded **53894** road segments this run (bbox includes off-island roads; 3.95M verts/94MB roads_coordinates) — vs the ~20642 from the polygon-clip path. Both are internally self-consistent (centerlines==mesh.data); the prompt's "only island" guideline would favor a polygon clip but all app1–4 trials use the string for consistency. Length "entirely in shaders/GPU" is NOT possible in stock UTK (no user GPU compute path; only `SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP` frag shader) — compute in numpy data layer, document the trade-off (same as count-in-radius). Live `utk start --data ./data` validated under `timeout`: `/getGrammar`,`/getLayer?layer=roads|roadLengthTheme|roadNoiseTheme`,`/files/roads_*`,`/main.js`,`/` all 200.
30	- **`knotOp`/`op` arithmetic is evaluated on the CPU, NOT in a shader**: the bundle does `operation.replaceAll("prevResult",...); eval(operation)` in JS. So UTK has **no user-programmable GPU compute path** — its only GPU-evaluated step is `SMOOTH_COLOR_MAP` mapping an already-known per-vertex scalar to colour in the fragment shader. A "compute geometric length entirely in shaders" requirement therefore can't be met by stock UTK; the faithful realisation is to compute the reduction in the Python data layer and let the GPU colour-map shader render it (document the trade-off, like "count within radius not expressible in grammar").
31	- **Browser OOM from OBJECTS-level plot knots on the buildings layer (app3)**: putting BOTH scatter axes (noise x + area y) as OBJECTS knots on the full-island `buildings` layer (~7.4M verts, 10141 comps) crashes the tab with the native "Out of Memory" page *while loading* (DevTools dies, no stack trace). Per-building triangulation is pure-Python and slow: ~8 it/s → full island ≈ 2–2.5 h one-time build. A small bbox (`[40.70,-74.015,40.71,-74.005]`) builds in <1 min for validation.

# Manhattan Buildings — Subway Accessibility (3D, pickable)

A **fully browser-side** (no backend) web application that renders a **3D map of
Manhattan buildings**, where each building is colored by the **number of subway
stations within a 500-meter radius** of its footprint. Every one of the five
base layers — **surface, water, parks, roads and buildings** — is **pickable**:
click an element to select it (it turns cyan), click again to deselect.

Everything — fetching OpenStreetMap data, parsing the subway CSV, the spatial
join, and the 3D rendering — happens in the browser. There is no server-side
code: the only "server" is Vite's static dev/preview server.

---

## What it does

1. **Loads the subway stations** from `public/subway_manhattan_clean.csv`
   (NYC Open Data), parsing the `GTFS Latitude` / `GTFS Longitude` columns.
2. **Loads OpenStreetMap base layers** for Manhattan via the **Overpass API** —
   buildings, roads, parks and water — in a *single* combined query (to respect
   Overpass rate limits) scoped to the **Manhattan Island** administrative area.
   A fifth **surface** layer (a single ground polygon spanning the data bounding
   box) is synthesised locally. The Overpass result is cached in **IndexedDB**,
   so subsequent loads are instant and do not re-hit Overpass.
3. **Counts stations within 500 m** of every building footprint centroid using a
   uniform spatial grid (each building only checks its 9 neighbouring cells) and
   an equirectangular distance approximation.
4. **Renders a 3D map** with [MapLibre GL](https://maplibre.org/) +
   [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/): extruded buildings colored on a perceptually
   uniform **Viridis** ramp (dark purple = few nearby stations, bright yellow =
   many), plus surface, water, parks, roads and subway-station markers.
5. **Picking on all five layers.** Each base layer is `pickable`; clicking a
   feature toggles its selection and repaints it cyan (`#00e5ff`). Selections
   are tracked per layer, so you can select elements across surface, water,
   parks, roads and buildings at the same time. Hovering any element shows a
   tooltip; hovering a station shows its name and routes.

All major steps log progress to the **browser console** (`[main]`, `[subway]`,
`[overpass]`, `[spatial]`, `[render]` prefixes) so the full pipeline can be
traced and diagnosed from the console alone.

---

## Requirements

- **Node.js 18+** and **npm**
- A modern browser with WebGL2 (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari)
- Internet access on first run (to reach the Overpass API). After the first
  successful load the OSM data is cached locally in IndexedDB.

---

## Run it

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies
npm install

# 2. Start the dev server (http://localhost:3005)
npm run dev
```

Then open **http://localhost:3005** in your browser. The status line in the
top-left panel reports progress; open the developer console to watch the full
log. The very first load fetches Manhattan from Overpass (this can take 10–60 s
depending on mirror load); later loads read from the IndexedDB cache.

### Production build & preview

```bash
# Type-check + bundle into dist/
npm run build

# Serve the production build on http://localhost:3005
npm run preview
```

### Type-check only

```bash
npm run typecheck
```

---

## How it works (architecture)

```
public/subway_manhattan_clean.csv   NYC Open Data subway stations (input)

src/
  main.ts        Orchestrates the pipeline + status/legend UI
  subway.ts      Fetches & parses the subway CSV (quoted-field CSV parser)
  overpass.ts    Single combined Overpass query + synthesised surface
                 + IndexedDB cache + backoff
  spatial.ts     Grid-accelerated "stations within 500 m" count per building
  render.ts      MapLibre base map + deck.gl layers (3D extruded buildings,
                 click-to-select picking on all five layers)
  types.ts       Shared GeoJSON / domain types
```

### Notes & design decisions

- **Picking on all five layers.** A module-level `Map<layerId, Set<id>>` holds
  the selection plus a `version` counter. Each layer's color accessor returns
  the cyan select color when the feature's id is in its set, otherwise its base
  / ramp color. A click toggles the id, bumps `version`, and re-sets the deck.gl
  overlay's `layers` (color accessors fire again via `updateTriggers`).
- **Synthesised surface layer.** OSM has no single cheap "Manhattan landmass"
  polygon, so the surface is one ground rectangle spanning the (2%-padded)
  bounding box of all fetched features. It is drawn first (bottom) and is fully
  pickable like the rest.
- **One Overpass query, with backoff.** Buildings, roads, parks and water are
  fetched in a single request to minimise the chance of an HTTP 429. The fetch
  rotates across three public Overpass mirrors with exponential backoff and
  retries on 429/504.
- **Manhattan Island scope.** The query uses the Manhattan borough
  administrative area (`area(3608398124)`) so results stay on the island rather
  than spilling into a loose bounding box.
- **IndexedDB cache.** The converted layers are stored under the key
  `manhattan-subway-osm-layers-v1`. To force a fresh fetch, clear the site's
  IndexedDB (DevTools → Application → IndexedDB → `manhattan-subway`) and reload.
- **500 m counting.** Distances are measured from each building's footprint
  centroid using an equirectangular approximation (sub-metre accurate at this
  scale and latitude). A ~500 m grid keeps the join near-linear.
- **Color encoding.** Building fill color maps `stationCount / max` through a
  Viridis ramp; the legend shows the `0 … mid … max` domain.

---

## Tech stack

- [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/) + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/) (base map / camera)
- [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/) `@deck.gl/mapbox`, `@deck.gl/layers`,
  `@deck.gl/core` (3D layers via `MapboxOverlay`)
- Data: [NYC Open Data](https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us/) (subway stations) +
  [OpenStreetMap](https://www.openstreetmap.org/) via the
  [Overpass API](https://overpass-api.de/)

- `spatial.ts` — grid-accelerated count of subway stations within 500 m of each building centroid (equirectangular metric, 9-cell neighbourhood).
- `render.ts` — MapLibre + deck.gl `MapboxOverlay`: extruded buildings on a Viridis ramp by station count, **click-to-select picking on all 5 layers** (surface, water, parks, roads, buildings) via a per-layer `Map<id,Set>` + `version` updateTrigger (selected → cyan), plus station markers and hover tooltips.
